topics.label: Introduction and lecture objectives
topics.groupedBecause: This subtopic frames the lecture within the cancer course and sets out its learning objectives.

topics.label: Cancer evolution and the origins of cancer-causing mutations
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics explain how mutations arise and enable susceptible cells to evolve into cancers within a permissive microenvironment.

topics.label: Environmental cancer risks and the evidence for their contribution
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics examine how evidence about environmental exposures informs judgments about whether cancer is caused or arises through chance.

topics.label: Infectious agents in cancer development
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics explain how infections contribute to cancer, with Burkitt lymphoma providing a detailed example of interacting infectious causes.

topics.label: Mechanisms of carcinogen-induced DNA damage
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics explain how environmental carcinogens produce DNA damage and mutations, including how bodily metabolism determines their activity.

topics.label: Tumour initiation and promotion
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics establish why mutation-bearing cells may require tumour-promoting conditions before they grow into cancers.

topics.label: Developmental and tissue-specific susceptibility to carcinogens
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics explain how the context of carcinogen exposure shapes susceptibility and consolidate the preceding account of carcinogenic mechanisms.

topics.label: Assessing carcinogen exposure and carcinogenicity
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics examine the methods available for connecting exposures to cancer and the limitations of the evidence those methods produce.

topics.label: Closing summary and risk–benefit decisions
topics.groupedBecause: This subtopic closes the lecture by summarising its conclusions and placing cancer risks within everyday risk–benefit decisions.
